$comment: What a reference search answers, as every implementation of the Librarian must answer it: a request, what each source the search reads answers, and the candidates in order, each with its score and the reason given for it. Semiont's Librarian (apps/librarian: reference_search.py) runs every case, in apps/librarian/tests/test_score_cases.py, and fails on a difference; a Librarian in another language runs the same file. WHAT A CASE STATES. `request` is the payload of `match:search-requested`. `now` is the moment the search is made: recency is counted from it, so a runner sets its clock to it. `resources` describes each resource the case names; a source that has a resource answers this description of it. `graph.byName` is what the graph's listing by name answers, as ids in the order it answers them, or `fails` with the failure's message. `graph.byEntityType` is what its listing by entity type answers; it is absent when that listing is not asked. `graph.byId` states, for each id the graph is asked to give the description of, whether the description is `held` or `absent`, or that the read `fails`. `views` states, for each id the view store is asked for, whether the view is `held` or `absent`. No other id is asked of either. `vectors` is what the vector index answers: its `hits` in the order it answers them, each a resource's id and a score, or `fails`; it is absent when the index is not asked. `model` is absent when the model is not asked. Otherwise `shown` is the ids of the candidates it is asked to score, in the order they are numbered from 1, and `answers` is the array of elements it answers, each a `candidate`, by its number, and a `score`, or `fails` says it does not answer. `term` is the search term the sources are asked with. `results` is the `response` of `match:search-results`: each candidate is the description of its resource with `score` and `matchReason` added, and a case states its id and those two. `failed` is the `error` of `match:search-failed`, and such a case states only what is needed to reach it. Either reply carries the request's `referenceId`. THE TERM is the focus's selected text and its hint, each left out when it is absent or empty, joined by one space. THE SOURCES. The graph's listing by name is asked for at most 20 resources by the term, whatever the term is. Its listing by entity type is asked for at most 50 resources of the context's entity types (`metadata.entityTypes`), and only when the context has any. The neighbours are the resources the context's graph connects the request's resource to: each is asked of the graph by id, and of the view store when the graph has none or its read fails; a neighbour neither holds is no candidate. The vector index is asked for at most 40 hits that score 0.4 or more against the embedding of the term, of chunks of any resource but the request's own, and only when the term is not blank: empty, or white space alone. An index that fails has answered no hits. Each hit's resource is read as a neighbour's is, and a hit neither store holds is no candidate. A resource is one candidate however many sources found it, and it is found by each source that answered it: by name, by entity type, as a neighbour, by the vector index. The request's own resource is no candidate, whichever source answers it. THE SCORE is the sum of these, rounded to two decimals. Entity types, only when the context and the candidate each have any: 30 times the types they share divided by the distinct types of both together, and for each shared type 5 divided by the base-2 logarithm of one more than the type's frequency (`metadata.entityTypeFrequencies`; a type with no stated frequency, or with one below 1, counts as seen once). Connection: 20 when the graph connects the request's resource to the candidate both ways, 10 when it connects it one way. Name, the candidate's name and the term compared without regard to the case of letters: 25 when they are equal, else 15 when the name begins with the term, else 10 when the name has the term in it; a blank term matches no name. Recency, for a candidate that states `dateCreated`: 5 times one less the candidate's age in days divided by 30, nothing from thirty days on, and nothing for a date after the moment of the search. Vector index: 25 times the hit's score, and of several hits of one resource the highest of their scores. What cites the request's resource adds nothing to any candidate. Several sources: 3 for each source that found the candidate, when more than one did. THE REASON is these, in this order, joined by `; `: `entity types: ` and the shared types in the context's order, joined by `, `; `bidirectional connection` or `connected`; `exact name match`, `prefix name match` or `contains name match`; `semantic similarity` for a vector hit; and the count of sources followed by ` retrieval sources`, when more than one found it. A candidate with none of these has the reason `candidate`. THE MODEL is asked once, unless the request states `useSemanticScoring` as false or there is no candidate. It is shown the twenty candidates of the highest scores, or all of them when there are fewer, numbered from 1 with the highest score first, and those of one score in the order they were found. Each score it gives a candidate it was shown adds 25 times that score, and the sum is rounded to two decimals again; a score above 0.5 adds `semantic match` to the reason, and is the whole reason of a candidate whose reason was `candidate`. A model that fails, or whose reply states no score, leaves the scores as they were. THE ORDER is by score, the highest first. Candidates of one score stay in the order they were found: the listing by name, the listing by entity type, the neighbours in the order of the graph's edges, the vector index's hits. When the request states a `limit`, the answer is that many of the first candidates at most. FAILURES. A focus that is not an annotation is answered on `match:search-failed`, and no source is asked. So is a search whose listing by name fails, with the failure's message. A `limit` is 1 to 200 by the request's schema, so no case states one outside it. What the prompt says and how a reply is read are not this table's. Add a case here before changing an implementation.

cases.why: a resource found by name alone, whose name is the term in other letter case, is an exact name match

a name equal to the term outranks one that begins with it, which outranks one that has it within, which outranks one found by name that has no such match: the answer is ordered by score and not as the listing answered
the term is the selected text and the hint joined by a space, and a name is matched against the whole of it
a focus with a hint and no selected text is searched by the hint alone
a focus with no selected text and no hint has the empty term: the listing by name is asked with it, the vector index is not asked, and with no candidate the model is not asked and the answer is empty
a term of white space alone is blank: the vector index is not asked, and a neighbour is still a candidate
a resource the graph connects the request's resource to one way is a candidate, and connected
a resource connected both ways scores twice what one connected one way does
two resources cite the request's resource, and no candidate gains from them: a neighbour scores what its connection gives it
a neighbour the graph does not hold yet is described from its view, and is a candidate all the same; made six days before the search, it gains 4 for recency
a neighbour whose read of the graph fails is described from its view
a neighbour neither the graph nor the view store holds is no candidate, and with no candidate the model is not asked
each hit of the vector index scores 25 times its own score: one the graph holds, one described from its view, and one neither holds, which is no candidate
a vector index that fails has answered no hits, and the search answers from its other sources
a resource found by two sources, by name and by the vector index, is one candidate and gains 3 for each source

results.matchReason: exact name match; semantic similarity; 2 retrieval sources

cases.why: a resource found by all four sources has every term of the score but recency, and its reason states them in their order

results.matchReason: entity types: Person; bidirectional connection; exact name match; semantic similarity; 4 retrieval sources

cases.why: a candidate with the context's one entity type, a type seen three times: 30 for the whole overlap and 2.5 for the type
an entity type the context states no frequency for counts as a type seen once, and adds 5

the overlap is the shared types over all the types of both, and a rare type weighs more than a common one: sharing the rare one of two outranks sharing the common one, sharing both outranks either, and types of its own that the context lacks lower a candidate
entity types add nothing to a candidate that shares none with the context, nor to one that has none
inside thirty days a newer resource gains more: 5 when it is made at the moment of the search, 4 at six days, 2.5 at fifteen
recency adds nothing to a resource made thirty days before the search, nor to one made forty-five days before it
recency adds nothing to a resource that states no date
a limit of two answers the two candidates of the highest score, and not the first two a source answered
a request that does not state `useSemanticScoring` has the model asked: each score adds 25 times itself, a score above 0.5 adds `semantic match` to the reason, and a score of 0.5 does not
the answer is ordered after the model's scores are added: the candidate that scored least before them is first
a model that fails leaves every score as it was, and the search still answers
a reply that states no score leaves every score as it was
a request that states `useSemanticScoring` as false has no model asked

of twenty-one candidates the model is shown twenty: a score it gives the twentieth counts, and an element of its reply numbered 21 names no candidate and adds nothing. Each candidate shares the context's one entity type, seen 31 times, for 31; they were made a day and a half apart, the first at the moment of the search, so recency gives the first 5 and each one after it a quarter less
two candidates of one score stay in the order they were found: the one the listing by name answered is before the neighbour
an empty term matches no name: a resource the listing by name answers for it has no name match, though every name begins with the empty text
a term of white space alone matches no name either: a name that has a space in it does not have the term in it
an entity type whose stated frequency is 0 counts as a type seen once, and adds 5
recency adds nothing to a resource whose date is after the moment of the search
of two hits of one resource the higher score counts, though the index answered the lower one last, and the resource is one candidate
the request's own resource is no candidate, though the listing by name and the listing by entity type each answer it
a score above 0.5 from the model is the whole reason of a candidate that had none: `semantic match`, with no `candidate` before it

the model is shown the twenty candidates of the highest scores, and not the first twenty found: of twenty-one the listing by name answers, the first has no name match and scores least, so the other twenty are shown, and the score the reply gives candidate 1 is the second one found's
a focus that is a resource, and not an annotation, is answered with a failure, and no source is asked
a search whose listing by name fails is answered with a failure that carries the listing's message
